🇲🇽🛢️ MEXICO ABSORBS THE OIL SPIKE SO DRIVERS DON'T

As global crude climbed, Hacienda raised the fuel subsidy for the week of July 11–17: the fiscal stimulus on Magna gasoline rose to 15.95% and on diesel to 26.26% — the highest of any fuel — with the state eating 1.06 and 1.93 pesos per liter through the IEPS "to keep fuel price increases from hitting consumers' wallets and feeding inflation." Premium, the luxury grade, gets no subsidy at all.

🇲🇽🤝 MEXICO CITY NEARS UNIVERSAL WELFARE FOR MEN 60–64

Clara Brugada's government added 20,000 men to the Hombres Bienestar program, which pays 3,000 pesos every two months to men aged 60 to 64 — the bridge years before the federal elderly pension begins. The program now covers 110,000 and is headed to 154,000 by year's end, a 1.7-billion-peso investment. One in every two men in that age bracket in the capital now receives the support.

🇲🇽📚 RECORD 58 BILLION PESOS FOR MEXICO'S SCHOOLS

Sheinbaum announced 58.4 billion pesos for school infrastructure in 2026 — "a historic investment for the country's schools," she said, "not counting what states invest directly." The bulk flows through La Escuela es Nuestra, which reached 71,482 schools this year by handing budgets straight to parent committees. The plan adds 156,240 new upper-secondary spots and 31 new national prep campuses, with 22 million students on welfare scholarships by year's end.

🔥🇲🇽 MEXICO'S BUSINESS COUNCIL PAID AN EX-CIA OFFICER TO LOBBY WASHINGTON

An investigation found the Consejo Mexicano de Negocios — the country's most powerful business lobby — paid the firm Continental Strategy $120,000 in 2025 to work the US State, Treasury, Homeland Security and Commerce departments. One of its three registered lobbyists: Enrique "Rick" de la Torre, a retired CIA operations officer with 25 years "in intelligence, diplomacy and international business." The firm is led by Carlos Trujillo, Trump's former ambassador to the OAS.

🇲🇽🌎 MEXICO MOVES TO CLEAN THE RIVERS NEOLIBERALISM POISONED

The federal government committed 7 billion pesos to sanitize the Lerma-Santiago basin, one of Mexico's three most contaminated rivers alongside the Atoyac and the Tula. Decades of unregulated industrial dumping turned the Santiago toxic — an NGO study linked its pollution to roughly 3,000 deaths over 18 years. Sheinbaum pledged to remediate all three, with 500 million pesos applied in 2025 and the balance running through 2030.

🚨🇲🇽 MEXICO DECLINES RUBIO'S SUMMIT TO BRAND THE LEFT AS "TERRORISTS"

Marco Rubio invited some 60 countries to a July 16 Washington summit against what he calls "transnational extreme-left terrorism." Mexico said no. Sheinbaum's government declined the invitation outright — Mexico and Brazil were singled out for special invites as the region's two largest left-led economies, precisely the governments a summit like this exists to target. Mexico won't lend its name to it.

🇲🇽✊ Money straight to the schools — no middlemen. "In 2026, 22.69 billion pesos go directly to 71,482 schools across the country." — Pamela López Ruiz, director of La Escuela es Nuestra, July 13 The program hands resources directly to school committees of parents and teachers, who set their own priorities. Under Sheinbaum it expanded to secondary and high schools, reaching 100% coverage there for 2025-2026, with primary and preschool targeted for 2027.

🇲🇽🏭 Mexican sugar wins back its US export quota. "The US is raising its import quota for Mexican sugar. This is excellent news." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, July 13 Mexico recovered its sugar export quota to the US market for this cycle and the next. Sugar is a strategic rural industry — thousands of cane-growing families depend on the export, and the restored quota brings certainty to the country’s mills.
